steps.text: Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until smooth and creamy. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Mix in vanilla.
Combine flours, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon in a separate bowl; stir into creamed mixture. Fold in oats and dates. Cover and chill dough in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.

Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease 2 baking sheets. Roll dough into walnut-sized balls and place 2 inches apart onto the prepared baking sheets. Flatten each cookie with a large fork.
Bake in the preheated oven until cookies are golden brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Cool cookies on the baking sheets for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Healthier Soft Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These healthy, chewy oatmeal cookies made with whole wheat flour, rolled oats, dates, and less sugar are a moist, tasty treat that's simple to make.

review.reviewBody: These are DELISH!!! I used 1/2 coconut oil, 1/2 unsweetened applesauce, and Stevia in place of sugar. I didn't use dates nor nuts----but some butterscotch chips I had left over. So yummy. I will make these again for sure.

I used "egg beaters" instead of the eggs. I also used "Smart Balance" 50/50 omega spread in place of butter. I used 1 c dark chocolate chips instead of the dates. And I didn't chill the dough, just dropped them by tablespoonful on the cookie sheet and didn't press them down. Baked them 8 minutes. They were absolutely great. Next time, I'll sub some of the butter for unsweetened applesauce, as others have suggested.

I loved the idea of a healthier oatmeal cookie recipe, so went ahead and made a little adjustments to this recipe hoping my family would like it. These are my changes: substituted butter with coconut oil, used 1 1/3 c brown sugar in place of both sugars, doubled the vanilla extract, reduced the all-purpose flour to 1/2 c, reduced the salt to 1/2 tsp, omitted the cinnamon and dates, and added 1 c chopped pecans and 1/2 c raisins. The rest of the ingredients (eggs, baking soda & whole wheat flour) were kept the same as the original recipe. My family loved these!! :) I try to always have these already rolled into balls in the freezer, so I can just take them out of the freezer to room temp while the oven gets to 375F and bake them for 12 minutes, this way they are done but still a bit chewy and just delicious. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

They were very good. I added pecans, coconut, dried cherries, and chocolate chips. I used half the sugar, only used the brown. I replace with half a banana and used only 1/2 cup of the butter and a half cup applesauce. Very moist and nice texture and sweet enough with the banana and applesauce.

These are great but I did make a few changes the last time I made them. I used 1/4 C white flour and 3/4 fine almond flour instead of 1 C wh. flour. I used about 2 C chopped dates and about 1 C of chopped walnuts too.

So here's what I did:

1) I added 1 cup of pecans to the mix
2) I did not chill the dough, just dropped it by teaspoonfuls onto the cookie sheet
3) Didn't press down the mounds of dough with a fork, just let them bake puffed up, and got a softer cookie

Everything worked out just great!
I made this except I subbed 1/2c applesauce and 1/2c olive oil for butter and raisins for dates. It turned out great. Here’s the nutrition facts:

These are very good! And I also feel good with this recipe as being a healthier version of greasier oatmeal cookies. And even with this being a lighter version I still cut out 1/4 cup of brown sugar and doubled on cinnamon and vanilla. Also added 1 cup or roasted walnuts that I roughly chopped up for my husband and on the 2nd batch I added 3/4 cup of roasted almonds roughly chopped for myself and my 5 year old daughter. This is a go to recipe when we crave oatmeal cookies!! :)

I substituted half the butter and all of the eggs with one cup of canned pumpkin puree(1/4 c per egg + 1/2 c for the butter). I used stevia instead of the white sugar. Next time I will cut back on the stevia just a little. It's a little bit too sweet and I can barely taste the stevia. But the cookies are delicious. I'd like a little nutmeg with the pumpkin too. It will make a yummy breakfast cookie. Also I used whole wheat pastry flour.

Definitely added to my list of top favourites as soon as I tasted them! I used some walnuts and raisins, but I will do without the raisins next time, as they tend to give a slightly sour taste. Also I didn't have whole flour and only used all-purpose. Kept the dough in the fridge for about 10 minutes only as I was short of time. A great recipe if you, like me, don't like spending much time in the kitchen but prefer home-made biscuits with your tea or coffee :)
I tried this recipe using 1/2 coconut oil and 1/2 natural peanut butter, then subbed out the white sugar for stevia, the white flour for coconut flour and the dates for mashed ripe banana. AMAZING!

They are soft and quick to make. I did not refrigerate the dough but using my cookie spoon I dropped roundfulls on the cookie sheet and flatten them with a fork. Instead of dates I used raisins and I didn’t have whole wheat and so I used white flour instead. My husband and I enjoyed a few with our hot chocolate. I will make them again.
Awesome recipe! I don’t use date. I add butterscotch chips, chocolate chips and walnuts. DELICIOUS
Very good. I used dried crandberries and macadamia nuts in place of dates
These were a tasty little cookie that was chewy and moist. I added a little chopped pecans as a personal preference. The chopped dates was a nice variation from raisins.
I did only 3/4 brown sugar. Used raisins instead of dates. Used all unbleached white flour.
Made as is. Turned out great.
excellent I made per recipe...
I added walnuts cause I love them and raisins perfect.
Used 1c Smarties instead of the dates. Super good! Had to adjust cooking time, but otherwise great cookies!
